title: Security Mechanisms, Protocols, and Incident Response
description: Prevention principles across OSI layers, security policies, network survivability, NSM, honeypots, testing methodologies (DREAD, STRIDE, OSSTMM), SANS incident-response steps, security protocols (IPSec, TLS/SSL, SSH, PGP), and wireless-specific security.
learning_objectives: Explain prevention measures at each OSI/TCP-IP layer
Describe how to develop a security policy (risk estimation, cost-benefit, standards)
State the basic security principles: simplify, reduce, harden, diversify, document
Describe survival properties: resistance, recognition, and adaptation
Explain the NSM process: detection, identification, validation, and short-term incident containment
Describe honeypots/honeynets and their role in intrusion observation
Apply risk-analysis methodologies: DREAD, OCTAVE, STRIDE, OSSTMM
Outline the six SANS incident-response steps
Describe IPSec services (Authentication Header, ESP) and its deployment in routers/firewalls
Explain the TLS handshake protocol, alert protocol, and session state
Describe SSH, PGP, and S/MIME at the application layer
Identify wireless threats and countermeasures (WEP weaknesses, WPA/WPA2/WPA3, WTLS)
